To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the size of fat cells in hypertensives was not different from those of controls.
the fat cell size of patients with essential hypertension is increased in obese hypertensives only.
the adipose cell size in hypertensive patients is not enlarged.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of a possible role of enlarged adipocytes in essential hypertension.
the question whether hypertensive patients have enlarged adipose cells and thus are predisposed to hyperlipoproteins.
the hypothesis that the hypertensive disease is a consequence of the metabolic disorder of the adipose tissue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adipose cell size is normal in essential hypertensives with normal weight and that it is increased in hypertensives of normal weight as well as of overweight.
the enlargement of adipocytes in patients with essential high blood pressure is secondary to the above-mentioned conditions.
hypertensive patients with obesity have an increased adipose cell volume and that this is due to a combination of increased adipose cell size and increased number of adipose cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hypertensive patients with overweight show an increase of adipose cell volume.
hypertensives with normal weight do not show any significant differences from normotensive controls, whereas hypertensives with obesity exhibit enlarged adipocytes and a tendency to increased HLP.
the hypertensive patient with normal body weight has a normal adipose cell volume, whereas in the hypertensive patient who is overweight the adipose tissue is hyperplastic and hypertriglyceridaemic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adipose cell size in hypertensive patients with normal body weight is not increased.
the adipose cell size is not enlarged in essential hypertension.
hypertensives have larger fat cells, which may be due to increased lipolysis and/or impaired insulin action in adipose tissue.
